name: PT Garuda Maintenance Facility Aero Asia Tbk

frontmatter.title: GMF AeroAsia - the dilution is behind it, the cash conversion is not
frontmatter.summary: A state-controlled aircraft maintenance franchise that has been recapitalised, priced as if the recapitalisation never happened. The share count multiplied through a land-inbreng rights issue and the price fell with it, while the enterprise kept earning. We are BUY: the balance sheet is fixed and the next test is converting group work into cash.
thesis: The price fall is dilution, not value destruction - the share count multiplied several times through the land-inbreng rights issue while market capitalisation rose.
Affiliate work from Garuda Group is the bulk of revenue and the parent is being recapitalised, so the revenue base is more secure than the tiny free float and the penny price suggest.

EBITDA is company-reported at a level the market is capitalising at a deep discount, and capex is a fraction of what an asset-heavy MRO would normally spend because the hangar land arrived by inbreng.
Net debt falls on our forecasts as free cash flow is applied to debt, and the payout policy is now legally possible after the retained-deficit clean-up.
The state's own November 2026 transfer valued the whole company far above the market price.

catalysts.event: Oman GMF Technic, the joint venture with Oman Air, starts full operations
FY2026 audited results against the company's own revenue and net profit targets
Flagged rights issue for free-float compliance - ratio, price and timing
Completion of Garuda's rights issue, which puts the controlling stake back under Garuda

blocks.text: GMF AeroAsia is a 5,205-person MRO provider based at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Tangerang [S0]. It reports three revenue segments: repair and overhaul, which was 79.3% of FY2025 revenue at US$390.0m; line maintenance, the daily and transit checks that shrank in FY2025; and other operations including defence and industrial services [S7]. The revenue mix is concentrated by customer rather than by service: Garuda Group affiliates supplied US$340.0m of FY2025 revenue against US$126.0m from non-affiliates, so roughly seven rupiah in ten come from companies under the same ultimate control [S7]. Commercial aviation was 75.4% of first-quarter 2026 revenue, the segment that carries the growth [S4].

The capability set is the moat argument. During 2025 the company added B737 MAX and B787 platform capability plus landing gear and aero-structure work, and it holds the certifications that let it serve foreign carriers [S7]. The hangars sit inside Indonesia's busiest airport, which is a real locational advantage for domestic airlines and a real constraint on growth: heavy maintenance capacity is fixed, so revenue growth has to come from higher utilisation and higher-value work rather than from new bays. The defence and engine shops diversify away from the civil aviation cycle [S7].

Growth beyond the home base is now explicit. In November 2026 GMF and Oman Air inaugurated Oman GMF Technic, an even-split joint venture at Muscat International Airport with two hangars, wide-body and narrow-body capacity, an adjustable docking system and a revenue target of US$44.0m a year from January 2027 [S5]. Because it is a joint venture its revenue is not consolidated; its value to GMFI is equity income plus the option on Middle East work, and we do not put its revenue in our consolidated line [S5].

Ownership has been rebuilt twice in two years. Garuda Indonesia began 2025 holding almost all of the company; during the year Angkasa Pura Indonesia took 65.8% through a non-cash rights issue in which land was contributed, leaving Garuda with a minority and the public with a sliver [S7]. In November 2026 Angkasa Pura transferred that stake to InJourney as a dividend in specie [S10], and Garuda's rights issue is designed to take it back through an inbreng from Danantara Asset Management [S6]. The direction of travel is a single aviation group under Danantara, with GMFI as its maintenance arm. That is strategically coherent and a governance concentration at the same time.

The global MRO market is forecast to grow at 2.8% a year to reach USD157bn by 2035, according to the Oliver Wyman forecast the company cites in its 2025 report [S7]. Indonesia should outgrow that: the domestic fleet is expanding, Garuda is reactivating aircraft, and regional maintenance capacity is short after years of under-investment. The binding constraint in 2025 was the supply chain - limited production capacity and late deliveries of materials and spare parts meant demand exceeded available supply, which is simultaneously a revenue ceiling and a margin problem [S7]. That constraint is the single best explanation of why a company with a captive customer base still reported a gross margin in the high teens for most of 2026 rather than the low twenties it earned in the good quarters of 2025 [S7].

Competition is national and regional. Domestically GMF is the incumbent with the only heavy-maintenance footprint at scale, which gives it a natural advantage for Indonesian carriers who do not want to fly aircraft abroad for checks. Regionally it competes with Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and the Gulf for third-party work, where price, turnaround time and certification decide. The company's own disclosure splits the market into affiliate and non-affiliate revenue because the two behave differently: affiliate work is contracted within the group, while non-affiliate work is won against regional MROs on commercial terms [S7]. The Oman joint venture is an attempt to compete in the Gulf on the Gulf's terms rather than exporting from Jakarta, and to qualify for the certifications that open that market [S5].

Five forces, in order of severity. Buyer power is high: a handful of airlines, with the controlling shareholder's own carriers taking most of the revenue, so pricing is negotiated inside a group rather than discovered in a market [S7]. Supplier power is high and rising: components and materials are scarce, and subcontracting is now the largest purchased input, having grown faster than revenue in FY2025 as engine work increased [S7]. Barriers to entry are moderately high - certifications, hangars and licensed engineers - which is why the franchise has lasted seven decades and why new capacity in Indonesia is slow to appear. Substitutes are limited for heavy checks; line maintenance is more contestable and is the segment that shrank. Rivalry is regional rather than local, so GMF's pricing is set by what a Singapore or Gulf shop would charge, adjusted for the inconvenience of the customer's aircraft being away longer.

The moat is therefore real but narrow: location, certifications and a captive customer base. It does not confer pricing power against that customer base, and the evidence is a gross margin that has moved with the supply-chain cycle rather than ratcheting upward [S7]. A narrow moat sets the fade assumption in the valuation section more than the growth assumption does: we assume the company holds share and earns a normal return on capital, not that it expands margins beyond its last good year.

The regulatory frame is permissive rather than restrictive. Maintenance organisations operate under civil-aviation approved maintenance organisation rules, and the company's ability to serve foreign carriers depends on holding the relevant approvals from the United States and European authorities as well as the local regulator [S7]. The Oman venture is pursuing the same approvals, which is the gate that determines whether a Gulf hangar can serve Western fleets [S5]. For GMFI the practical regulatory risk is certification loss or suspension, which would be severe but is not a live issue today.

Aircraft heavy maintenance is a schedule-driven business: airframes come due for major checks at fixed
intervals, so an MRO's revenue is a function of the fleet's age and flight hours, not of the airline
cycle alone. That gives visibility but also means that a fleet reactivation delay moves revenue by
quarters, and that capacity, once built, is sticky. Airlines typically keep a primary and a backup
maintenance provider for each fleet type, so a shop that loses an approval loses the whole allocation,
not a share of it.

Revenue grew from US$238.7m in FY2022 to US$491.9m in FY2025 as Indonesian aviation recovered from the pandemic, more than doubling over three years [S7]. Operating income rose from US$42.0m to US$60.6m over the two audited years and net profit attributable to shareholders to US$33.9m [S11]. The nine-month 2026 figures are US$413.4m of revenue, US$57.4m of EBITDA and US$22.1m of net profit [S3].

Two corrections to the data pack matter. First, the pack overstates FY2025 operating income; the audited accounts report operating income of US$60.6m on total operating expenses of US$431.3m, against the US$42.0m and smaller expense block the pack carries for the prior year [S11]. We restate FY2024 and FY2025 revenue, operating income, D&A, net profit and capex from the filing, and the model rebuilds EBITDA from them: US$79.9m against the US$80.2m management reported [S4]. Second, the pack's D&A line is incomplete in FY2025; the notes give US$19.3m for FY2025 against US$18.7m for FY2024, and those are the figures the model uses [S11]. Without that restatement the model would carry a cash-cost base that is too high and an EBITDA that is too low. We confine our historical claims to the two restated years: the audited five-year summary does show positive operating income in FY2022 and FY2023, but its thousands-separated columns are not machine-readable in the archive, so pre-2024 levels in the model's history table are the pack's and we do not quote them [S7 p.18].

Margins are the heart of the forecast, and the honest place to start is that GMFI does not report a gross profit. The audited consolidated income statement runs revenue of US$491.9m straight into a single operating-expense block of US$431.3m - employee expenses [F32], materials [F33], subcontract [F34], depreciation [F8], operational expenses [F35] and other operating expenses [F36] - and then to operating income of US$60.6m [S11 p.18]. There is no Pokok Pendapatan line anywhere in the filing. Every "gross margin" this house prints for GMFI, including the nine-month figure that used to anchor this section, is therefore a derived split, not a filing fact: the pack allocates the operating-expense block into cost of revenue and SG&A, and that allocation is a vendor construct with no Q3-2026 LK behind it - the company's investor-relations page still ends at the 30 June 2026 interim [S2].

We now run the model on the audited basis and say so. Cost of revenue is the four direct production lines the notes disclose; SG&A is the two remaining audited lines. On FY2025 that split reproduces the audited operating income exactly, at a gross margin in the high teens, and 7.7% of SG&A, and it reproduces audited operating income exactly. The FY2026E margin is then derived from the only 2026 figure that is sourced - nine-month EBITDA of US$57.4m on US$413.4m of revenue [S3] - with D&A at 3.9% and SG&A at the audited rate, giving 17.8%. That is lower than the FY2025 level because the nine-month actual is lower, and it gives the December quarter no margin above the FY2025 peak: the fourth quarter at the nine-month margin is exactly what the model assumes.

Revenue follows the same discipline. Nine months are actual [S3][S8] and the fourth quarter is US$491.9m less the nine-month figure of last year - that is, no growth on the FY2025 December quarter and no seasonal uplift - which gives US$598.2m, about a tenth above the company's own US$542.8m target [S4]. That ratio is not a stretch: FY2025 revenue landed a tenth above the target the company set for it, and profit a quarter above [S7 p.32]. The June target, taken literally, would require a December quarter a third smaller than the one a year earlier, in the quarter the accounts show as the largest of the year, with nothing in the reactivation or contract disclosure to explain it.

Capex is the most unusual line in the model. Cash capex was US$4.6m in FY2025 and US$4.2m in FY2024, under one per cent of revenue, because the land under the hangars came in by inbreng rather than purchase [S7]. We lift it to 1.2% of revenue in FY2026E and 1.5% in FY2027E to fund the platform capabilities and the Oman venture, which is still an asset-light number for an MRO and is a key reason free cash flow is large relative to the market capitalisation [S5]. If capex instead normalises toward the depreciation charge, the cash-flow case weakens materially - that is one of our signposts.

Working capital is where the earnings-quality question sits. Operating working capital was US$-18.1m at end-2025 and turned positive by September 2026 as receivables rose to about two months of revenue, concentrated in Garuda and Citilink [S0][S8]. Operating cash flow through September was a fraction of net profit [S0]. The earnings-quality screen is run on the three-year numbers, not asserted: net profit less operating cash flow over average total assets was negative in two of the last three years and single-digit throughout, receivables grew slower than revenue over those three years, and the cash conversion of the first nine months of 2026 is the one number that has broken down - the calculation is set out line by line in the assumptions file so a reader can rebuild it. Cash conversion, not the accruals level, is the flag: the counterparty is the controlling shareholder, and a receivable that does not collect is an impairment, not a timing difference. That is why the bear case writes off a sixth of the receivable book rather than only stretching working capital.

The balance sheet was rebuilt. Equity went from US$-258.1m at end-2024 to US$114.4m at end-2025 after the land inbreng [S0], gross debt fell to US$384.8m and net debt to US$343.7m [S0]. On our forecasts net debt falls to US$255.3m in FY2027E and US$77.5m by FY2030E, which is 0.7x EBITDA, because free cash flow is applied to debt rather than to acquisitions [S7]. Capital allocation is therefore simple: deleverage, then distribute. The policy cap is 30.0% of profit and nothing has been paid since listing, and the balance sheet still carried an unappropriated accumulated deficit of US$523.1m at 31 December 2025 [S11 p.17]. The quasi-reorganisation that would clear it appears in the 2025 report as a plan put to the board committee in December 2025, not as a completed transaction [S7 p.272]. One dividend path therefore runs through this report: zero payout in FY2026E because no distribution can be declared against that deficit, then the full 30.0% cap from FY2027E. The template pays a year's declared dividend in the following year, which is why FY2026E dividends paid are zero and the target carries no next-twelve-month DPS.

A note on the shape of the forecast [S7]. FY2026E is nearly a reported year: nine months are actual and the fourth quarter is the company's own target. FY2027E is the first genuinely uncertain year, because it combines the completion of Garuda's reactivation with the start of the Oman joint venture. We grow revenue 9.0% that year and fade the rate to 5.0% by FY2030E, which is above the global market rate because Indonesia starts from a lower base, then 5.0% from FY2031E onward. The terminal growth in the DCF is lower still, at 2.5%, and the fade to it is deliberate: the explicit forecast carries the volume leverage, the perpetuity carries almost none.

We value GMFI on a ten-year FCFF discounted-cash-flow model, weighted entirely to that method. The choice is deliberate. There is no listed Indonesian MRO peer, and the company's own multiple history is unusable: the share count changed from 47,386 million to 124,836 million against a negative equity base, so the historical P/E and P/BV series mix two different companies and a meaningless per-share denominator. A peer median drawn from shipping and airline names would import a trough multiple onto a business at a trough margin, which is the error we are trying to avoid rather than repeat. The multiple tables below are shown as cross-checks only; they carry no weight in the target.

The discount rate is the engine's Indonesian build, and here is the arithmetic rather than a reference to it. The risk-free rate is 5.1%, the mature-market equity premium 4.2% and the country premium 2.5%. The unlevered beta of 0.90 is the industry regression; levered at the market debt-to-equity of 1.24 it is 1.77. The cost of equity applies the beta to the sum of the equity premium and the country premium - 5.1% plus 1.77 times (4.2% plus 2.5%) - giving 16.9%. Debt is priced at 7.1% pre-tax, which is the risk-free rate plus the corporate spread, at a 22.0% marginal rate; with equity at 44.7% and debt at 55.3% the WACC is 10.6%.

Two things the red team asked to have out in the open. First, the country premium is scaled by the levered beta in that formula. The additive form - the premium added once, unscaled - would give a cost of equity about two points lower and, at the same weights, a WACC near the top of the house band for USD names. We keep the scaled form because it is the engine's house build and because it is the more conservative of the two: the grid below shows what the value does at a WACC one point lower, so the reader can see how much of the target depends on the choice. It is not a defence of a high rate at any price - it is a statement that a small-cap MRO with related-party revenue, a 6.5% float and dollar debt against a thin equity base should not be discounted at the bottom of the band. Second, the model charges interest at 5.0%, the observed FY2025 rate on the debt actually outstanding, while the WACC uses 7.1%, the marginal cost of new debt. The two are consistent by design: the interest line prices the balance sheet as it is, the discount rate prices cash flows that would be financed at today's spread.

The DCF produces an enterprise value of US$1,079.6m for the operating business, of which the terminal value is 50.8%, and a value per share of Rp108 [S0]. That is the DCF value. Rolled twelve months forward at the cost of equity it becomes the base scenario, Rp126, and the probability-weighted blend of the three scenarios set out in section five is the Rp125 target. One chain, three numbers: DCF, base case, weighted target - the old draft described the roll and the blend as if they were two different builds, and they are not.

The multiple-survival test is the check that matters here, and it is run, not asserted. The terminal value is struck on FY2035E EBITDA of US$138.3m [S0] at an implied exit multiple a little under ten times. The entry is 7.2x FY2026E EV/EBITDA at Rp42 today, so the exit sits about four-tenths above entry - a real expansion, not a rounding difference, and the 50.8% of enterprise value the terminal value carries says how much of the target rests on it. We disclose it rather than bury it in total enterprise value, which is what the previous draft did. The defence is not that the market price is wrong in the abstract: the entry multiple is depressed by a rock-bottom float, a pending dilutive issue and a controlling-shareholder overhang that the exit year does not have. The harder anchor is the state's own November 2026 transaction, in which Angkasa Pura transferred 65.8% of GMFI to InJourney for IDR5.66tn [S10]: on our FY2026E EBITDA that implies about nine and a third times for the whole of the company - between the market's entry multiple and our implied exit, and paid by informed owners within the last fortnight. If a buyer paid only the entry multiple at exit, the DCF value per share would fall by about a fifth; that is the size of the multiple bet, and it is a fifth we accept on the transfer anchor, not one we leave the reader to discover.

The cross-checks disagree in an informative way. At Rp42 the market pays 7.2x FY2026E EV/EBITDA, 8.2x P/E, 1.9x P/BV and gets a 10.6% FCFE yield, rising to 19.8% next year. Our DCF value per share is Rp126 against a market capitalisation of IDR5,243.1bn [S0]. Between the two sits the most useful third data point: in November 2026 Angkasa Pura transferred 65.8% of GMFI to InJourney for IDR5.66tn, which values the whole company far above the market price and below our DCF [S10]. The state's own transaction price is an administered, related-party number, so it is neither fair value nor a floor; it is evidence that the market price is not the price informed owners put on the asset.

What today's price implies is now a solver output, not an inference. Holding the discount rate and the margin path, the engine's reverse-DCF solver on FY2027E revenue growth says today's Rp42 is consistent with revenue growth -7.6% below our base in that year and every year after - not a slower recovery but a franchise that shrinks relative to the recovery already visible in the nine-month actual. We also read the implication off the multiples: a 10.6% FCFE yield on a company with net debt of 3.7x EBITDA falling to 0.7x and no maturity wall is pricing governance and dilution risk, not solvency risk. We think the market is right to charge something for those risks and wrong to charge this much.

Sensitivity is concentrated in three inputs: revenue growth, gross margin and the discount rate. A two point change in revenue growth moves the value by roughly a tenth, a one point change in gross margin by a similar amount, and a one point change in WACC by about as much again. The rating survives a one-point higher WACC and a one-point lower margin at the same time, which is the test we care about; it does not survive a permanent step down in the gross margin to the nine-month 2026 level.

**Related-party dependence - likelihood high, impact high.** US$340.0m of US$491.9m FY2025 revenue came from Garuda Group affiliates, and Garuda itself is loss-making and raising equity [S7][S8]. A parent that pays late transfers its own liquidity problem to GMFI's receivables, which already stand at about two months of revenue [S0]. This is the risk that most deserves the discount the market is applying, and it is the one we cannot diversify away inside the position.

**Dilution and free float - likelihood high, impact medium.** The public holds a sliver of the shares and the free float is 6.5%, below the exchange requirement; a rights issue of 17.6% of capital has been flagged with no ratio, price or date [S8]. We do not wave that away as value-neutral. Issuing a fifth more shares at a price anywhere near Rp42 - about three-fifths below the DCF value per share - transfers value from existing holders to the subscribers, which is why the base case carries a probability-weighted bridge deduction for the dilution net of the cash raised, and why the bear case has the issue landing at a discount. If it is priced at or above intrinsic it is accretive and the deduction reverses; that asymmetry is why the catalyst list carries it.

**Governance and control - likelihood medium, impact high.** The controlling stake has moved twice in a year at administered values - Angkasa Pura to InJourney for IDR5.66tn, then into Garuda's rights issue [S10][S6]. Minority holders have no say over transfer pricing inside the group, and the deficit-clearing reorganisation, when it comes, will be decided by that same majority [S7 p.272]. We treat related-party terms as given, not negotiable, and we do not assume any improvement in them.

**Currency - likelihood medium, impact medium.** Gross debt of US$384.8m against equity of US$114.4m means a rupiah move hits the equity disproportionately, and the house macro deck has the rupiah at 18,350 by FY2027E. The company hedges its exposure and the revenue is dollar-denominated, which is the natural offset, but the balance sheet remains the transmission channel [S7].

**Operational - likelihood medium, impact medium.** Heavy maintenance is concentrated at a single airport, supply-chain delays for parts recur, and the subcontract line is the first thing to inflate when the supply chain tightens [S7]. The Oman joint venture adds execution risk in a new jurisdiction from January 2027, and an even-split structure means GMFI does not control it [S5].

**Liquidity and float - likelihood medium, impact high.** Three-month average daily turnover is IDR5.1bn on a 6.5% float, so an institutional position cannot be built or exited quickly [S0]. The float figure is the IDX registry measure carried in the data pack, and it is far below the exchange's free-float requirement - which is the stated reason for the flagged rights issue. On the exchange status the earnings-quality card requires us to check: the name is not on the special-monitoring board in the registry mirror we can see [S0], and we found no B, E, L, M or S notation disclosure in the filings we archived [S11]. That is a check, not a clearance. If the name were moved to the special-monitoring board the consequence would be full call auction, which would break the entry and exit assumptions outright on a float this thin, and no liquidity discount can fix that. We apply no liquidity discount because turnover is above the house threshold [S0], but we size the position against the float, not the market capitalisation: at this float a position of any institutional size is a governance bet with an exit problem attached.

The bear case has Garuda's restructuring stalling, affiliate revenue slipping, a sixth of the receivable book written off under PSAK 71, the rights issue landing at a discount and working capital absorbing cash; its twelve-month value is Rp73. The bull case has the reactivation accelerating, Oman ramping and margin leverage, worth Rp199; the base is Rp126. The probabilities are 50.0% base, 30.0% bear and 20.0% bull, and those three values weight to the Rp125 target in the investment summary - the same run, the same tokens, no separate arithmetic. The two tails shock the same three drivers by mirrored amounts - three points of revenue growth, one and a half points of gross margin and two points of working capital each way - and because the bull and the bear are roughly equidistant from the base in value terms, the weighting adds almost nothing to the base case on its own: the target is close to the base scenario, and the up-tail contributes about a third of it, not half. The bear carries the higher weight because the downside needs only that Garuda's recapitalisation stalls, while the bull needs reactivation, Oman and margin leverage together; the residual asymmetry in value is the fixed dilution bridge and the net debt, which bite harder when equity value is low. The impairment sits in the bear narrative and is more than covered by one and a half points of gross margin over ten years, which is a larger present-value hit than a single-year write-off of that size.

Signposts that would change our view: a quarterly decline in affiliate revenue; receivables days moving above three months or a PSAK 71 charge in a quarterly filing; a rights issue priced below the prevailing market price; the loss of a major third-party or defence contract; and any change in the dividend policy before the FY2026 results.

Ownership is the defining feature. A 65.8% controlling stake sat with Angkasa Pura at the end of FY2025, with Garuda holding a minority and the public a sliver [S7]; in November 2026 that block moved to InJourney as a dividend in specie [S10] and is destined for Garuda through the Danantara inbreng [S6]. The practical consequence is that GMFI's customer, supplier of capital and controlling shareholder are the same group. Related-party revenue of US$340.0m on US$491.9m of revenue is the number to hold in mind when reading any margin: group pricing can move value between GMFI and its parent without a visible transaction, and the auditor's related-party note is the only place it appears.

The free float is 6.5% [S0], below the exchange minimum, and closing that gap is the stated reason for the flagged rights issue [S8]. Until it is done, the shares are a controlled company with a public quotation rather than a genuinely traded equity. We found no pledge of the controlling stake disclosed in the 2025 report and no indication of multiple-voting shares [S7]; the stake transfer was expressly stated to be ordinary shares, not shares with multiple voting rights [S10].

Dividends have never been paid. The policy allows up to 30.0% of profit, but an unappropriated accumulated deficit of US$523.1m was still on the balance sheet at 31 December 2025 [S11 p.17], and the quasi-reorganisation that would clear it was a plan before the board committee in December 2025 [S7 p.272] rather than a completed transaction we can source. We therefore model zero payout in FY2026E and the full cap from FY2027E - one path, stated once. A first dividend is the single clearest signal that the recapitalisation has changed the company's relationship with its minorities, and until it is declared we do not assume it.

Board and management are state-appointed: Andi Fahrurrozi is president director and Tri Hartono finance director [S0]. The FY2025 accounts are audited and we restate our history from them. The integrated report discloses TCFD-aligned climate risk work and GRI-based sustainability reporting, and it identifies physical risk to the hangars and the transition risk from aviation decarbonisation as the material environmental exposures [S7]. The social exposure is the licensed-engineer workforce; the governance exposure is the related-party structure described above. None of these is currently a valuation driver beyond the discount rate; all of them are monitoring items.

The dated catalysts are the completion of Garuda's rights issue in November 2026, which settles GMFI's ownership [S6]; the Oman GMF Technic start-up in January 2027 [S5]; the FY2026 audited results in February 2027 against the US$542.8m revenue and US$34.5m net profit targets [S4]; and the flagged rights issue for free-float compliance, whose ratio and price will determine the next per-share step [S8].

Between updates we monitor five numbers. Affiliate revenue and its share of the total, because it is both the growth engine and the governance risk [S7]. Receivable days, because a rise past three months would turn a collection issue into a credit issue [S0]. The gross margin excluding subcontract, because that separates pricing from pass-through [S7]. Capex as a share of revenue, because a step toward the depreciation charge would break the free-cash-flow case [S7]. And net debt/EBITDA, which our forecast takes to 0.7x by FY2030E but which only falls if the cash actually arrives [S0].

bear.narrative: Garuda Group's restructuring stalls and the parent - loss-making and itself issuing equity - pays late: affiliate revenue slips as aircraft reactivation is deferred, and 15% of the USD92.3m receivable book (about USD13.8m) is written off under PSAK 71 because Garuda and Citilink together owe most of it and Garuda's recapitalisation is not closed. The flagged 17.6% free-float rights issue lands at a discount and takes per-share value with it. Revenue growth runs 3 points below base, gross margin gives back one and a half points to supply-chain and labour costs - in present-value terms a far larger hit than the one-off impairment - and working capital swings 2 points of revenue against us.

bull.narrative: Garuda's Rp16.9trn rights issue closes, the fleet reactivation accelerates and defence plus engine work fills the hangars; Oman GMF Technic ramps from January 2027 and GMF takes share as regional capacity stays short. Revenue growth runs 3 points above base, gross margin gains one and a half points on volume leverage, and collections normalise so working capital releases 2 points of revenue.

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the actual, not from the June-2026 target: nine months are reported at USD413.42m [S3][S8] and we add a fourth quarter of USD184.75m - exactly the FY2025 December quarter, no growth and no seasonal uplift - for USD598.17m, i.e. 110% of the company's USD542.79m target [S4]. That ratio is the company's own record: FY2025 revenue landed at 109% of its target [S7 p.32]. The target as printed would require a Q4 of USD129.4m, a 30% year-on-year fall in the quarter that was FY2025's largest, and nothing in the reactivation, contract or hangar-slot disclosure supports a break of that size [S7]. FY2027-28E grow 9% and 8% as the Garuda Group reactivation completes and the Oman JV starts contributing from January 2027 [S5]; FY2029-30E fade to 6% and 5%, above the 2.8% global MRO market rate [S7], then 4% long run, in line with USD nominal GDP.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: This input is a derived split, not a reported line: GMFI's audited consolidated income statement has no cost-of-revenue and no gross-profit line - revenue of USD491.88m is followed directly by a single operating-expense block of USD431.31m and operating income of USD60.57m [S11 p.18][F30]. We define cost of revenue as the four direct production lines the notes disclose - employee USD120.86m, material USD144.81m, subcontract USD108.62m and depreciation USD19.33m [F32][F33][F34] - which gives a 2025 margin of 19.98%, and put the two remaining audited lines (operational USD32.30m and other operating USD5.39m [F35][F36]) into opex. FY2026E is then derived from the sourced EBITDA instead: nine-month EBITDA of USD57.40m on USD413.42m of revenue is 13.9% [S3], and with D&A at the audited 3.93% of revenue [F8] and SG&A at 7.66% the implied margin is 17.7% - the fourth quarter is not given a peak margin above FY2025's. FY2027-30E recover 0.3-0.9 points as the D&A ratio drifts down and volume leverage comes through, but never back to the audited 2025 level, on the leverage the accounts themselves show (operating expenses fell from 90.0% of revenue in FY2024 to 87.7% in FY2025 as revenue grew 16.8%) [S11].

assumptions.label: SG&A and other operating expenses / revenue
assumptions.basis: On the audited definition this line is the two non-production operating-expense items: operational expenses of USD32.30m plus other operating expenses net of USD5.39m, USD37.69m or 7.66% of FY2025 revenue [F35][F36][S11 p.18]. Held at 7.66% through the forecast - no operating-leverage credit on this line, because the leverage is taken in the gross-margin line where the accounts show it.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Depreciation, amortisation and impairment were USD19.33m in FY2025 and USD18.69m in FY2024 per the notes to the audited accounts [S7], so the audited charge is 19.33/491.88 = 3.93% of revenue [F8]. The nine-month 2026 LK we hold reports revenue, EBITDA and net profit only - it carries no operating-income and no D&A line [S3] - so this ratio is set from the audited year, not from a subtraction of one unsourced figure from another. The FY2025 rise in fixed assets was non-cash land received from Angkasa Pura, so D&A does not step up with it; capex at 1.2-1.5% of revenue sits below the charge, so the ratio drifts down gently as revenue grows.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash capex was only USD4.61m in FY2025 and USD4.20m in FY2024 (0.9-1.0% of revenue) because the land under the hangars arrived by inbreng rather than purchase [S7]. FY2026-28E lift to 1.2-1.5% to fund the capability build the company names (737 MAX and 787 platforms, landing gear and aero structure) and the 50:50 Oman hangar JV from January 2027 [S5][S7]; back to 1.2% long run.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Working capital was negative USD18.2m at end-2025 (-3.7% of revenue) but swung to positive USD4.5m at 30 September 2026 as receivables rose to USD92.3m, 2.0 months of revenue, mostly from Garuda and Citilink [S0][S8]. The base case holds working capital at +0.5% of revenue - the last actual direction - and assumes no release; it does not extrapolate the FY2025 negative ratio.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Effective tax was 16.6% in FY2025 (tax USD6.76m on pre-tax profit USD40.73m) [S7]; the small permanent differences are stable. The 10% engine default comes from averaging a negative tax year and is not the rate being paid.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Finance costs were USD20.21m in FY2025 on average gross debt of about USD410m, 4.9%, mostly USD-denominated bank facilities and notes with hedges on the rupiah exposure [S7]. 5.0% is the current run-rate; no refinancing gain is assumed.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest income was USD0.89m in FY2025 on an average cash balance near USD27m, roughly 3.3%; the cash balance is small and held largely in USD [S7]. 3.5% is the observed yield, not the engine's default.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Gross debt moved from USD436.5m at end-2024 to USD384.8m at end-2025 and USD358.7m at 30 September 2026: the company is deleveraging with free cash flow, not borrowing [S0]. The base case assumes no new net debt, which leaves headroom unspent rather than inventing a refinancing.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2025 other income and expense was a net USD19.84m charge, of which USD20.21m was interest, so the residual is close to zero; FY2024 was a net positive. FX losses recur as the rupiah weakens but the company runs a hedging programme, so the base case carries no structural FX drag [S7].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interests took USD0.02m of FY2025 net profit and the minority balance sheet is USD0.19m; immaterial and held at zero [S7].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: One path, used in the assumptions, the model and the report: company policy permits up to 30% of the year's profit [F23], but the balance sheet still carried an unappropriated accumulated deficit of USD523.05m at 31 December 2025 [F37][S11 p.17], so no distribution can be declared out of FY2026E profit. The quasi-reorganisation that would clear it was still a plan when the 2025 report was printed [S7 p.272], so we model zero payout in FY2026E and the full 30% cap from FY2027E. Note the template's convention: dividends_paid in a year is the prior year's declared DPS times the share count, which is why FY2027E paid is zero against a 30% payout input, and the target's next-12-month DPS is accordingly zero rather than a modelled FY2026E dividend.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The count was 120,022m at 31 December 2025 and the land-inbreng rights issue completed on 27 January 2026 took it to 124,835m, so FY2026E carries that 4.0% step and nothing after it [S7]. The flagged free-float rights issue of about 17.6% [F29] has no approved ratio, price or timetable, so the base case does not issue shares; it is modelled where it belongs - as dilution in the bear case (a.share_change +17.6% in FY2026E) and as a probability-weighted bridge deduction for the difference between the intrinsic value and the issue price.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: USD-reported revenue from an Indonesian MRO franchise: 2.5% is below the 4% USD nominal GDP path and above the 2.8% global MRO market rate the company cites [S7], consistent with a business that holds share but not pricing power.

challenges.challenge: The 17.7% 9M-2026 gross margin and the 23.1% Q4-2025 gross margin anchor the whole 19.0-19.8% path, but neither is in an archived source: S3 carries revenue, EBITDA and net profit only; S8 carries revenue by segment; S7 shows a single Beban Usaha line of 431.31m with no cost-of-revenue split and no Pokok Pendapatan line anywhere; S0 has no archived text. The report presents the USD387.57m cost of revenue as a filing fact when it is a pack construct.
challenges.answer: The 17.7% 9M margin is gone from model and report: no Q3-2026 LK exists (IR page ends at the 30 June 2026 interim, S2) and the audited P&L has no cost-of-revenue line at all (S11 p.18: revenue then one USD431.31m operating-expense block). The forecast margin is derived from sourced 9M EBITDA of USD57.40m on USD413.42m (S3) with the audited opex ratio, and the report says the gross-profit split is a derived construct. Added audited component facts F30-F36.

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test is asserted, not run: terminal value of 1,302.8m on 2035 EBITDA of 130.5m is an exit multiple of 9.98x against the 7.46x FY2026E entry multiple the report itself quotes - 34% expansion - while section 4 says we are not assuming multiple expansion. The card requires the implied exit versus entry multiple to be stated.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the terminal value and FY2035E EBITDA as tokens so the implied exit multiple is visible against the FY2026E entry multiple, and justifies it against the state's own 2 November 2026 transfer (Rp5.66trn for 65.77%) rather than asserting survival. It discloses that a 7.5x exit would cut value per share by about a tenth.

challenges.challenge: The scenario table resolves to bear Rp31 and bull Rp247, which weight with a Rp121 base to Rp130 - not the Rp141 target, which requires the Rp35/Rp286 pair the packet shows. The prose hands the reader a different valuation from the one that was signed off, and section 5 is where the rating is defended.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now resolves the three scenario target values (not the pre-roll v0s) and states that they weight to val.tp_final, so the prose arithmetic and the signed-off target are the same run; the probabilities are re-rendered from the model.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E base of 542.79m is a 10 June 2026 target: with 9M revenue of 413.42m (S3/S8) it implies Q4 of 129.4m against the 184.75m of Q4 2025 (491.88 less 9M 307.13) - a 30% year-on-year fall in the quarter the report calls seasonally the strongest, with no capacity, contract or schedule source for the break.
challenges.answer: FY2026E revenue rebuilt from the actual: 9M of USD413.42m (S3) plus a Q4 equal to FY2025's own December quarter, i.e. USD598.17m, about a tenth above the June target and in line with the company's 109%-of-target FY2025 record (S7 p.32).

challenges.challenge: At 19.0% FY2026E gross margin, FY gross profit is 103.1m against 73.2m for 9M, so Q4 gross margin must be 23.2% - above the 23.1% Q4 2025 the report calls an exceptional peak and says the model does not return to. The narrative and the arithmetic describe different forecasts.
challenges.answer: Consistent now: the FY2026E gross margin is derived from the sourced 9M EBITDA margin, so Q4 carries the nine-month margin, not a peak above Q4 2025. The 23.2% implied Q4 is gone with the 19.0% input.

challenges.challenge: The 16.9% COE is produced by scaling the 2.5% country premium by the 1.78 levered beta (5.0 + 1.78 x (4.2 + 2.5)); the standard additive form gives 14.97% and, at the same 44.5/55.5 weights, a 9.69% WACC - inside the 8-10% house band for USD names. The confessed band breach therefore rests on an undisclosed build choice, and the model charges interest at 5.0% while the WACC uses 7.0% pre-tax.
challenges.answer: The COE formula is written out in section 4 (rf plus levered beta times ERP plus CRP), the additive-CRP alternative is disclosed and cross-referenced to the sensitivity grid, and the two debt costs are reconciled: 5.0% observed on the existing debt in the P&L, 7.1% marginal in the WACC.

challenges.challenge: The 17.6% rights issue is called high likelihood in section 5, yet shares stay at 124,836m to FY2035, the bridge is empty, and the bear narrative says the issue lands at a discount while none of the three bear shocks touches the share count. At Rp42 the issue adds roughly 22.0bn shares and USD50m of cash, taking DCF value per share from Rp105 to about Rp96.
challenges.answer: The issue is now modelled: a probability-weighted bridge deduction of USD62m for dilution net of the cash raised (17.6% new shares at a price near Rp42 against an intrinsic value more than twice it) and the bear narrative carries it. Base share count unchanged because no ratio, price or date is approved.

challenges.challenge: S7 p.32 records FY2025 revenue at 109% and profit at 125% of the company own target. That track record is direct evidence the June 2026 target used as the base is conservative - consistent with the Q4 arithmetic above - and the report never uses it.
challenges.answer: The target-beat record is now a driver: FY2025 revenue landed a tenth above target and profit a quarter above (S7 p.32), which is the sourced reason FY2026E carries USD598m against the June target of USD542.79m.

challenges.challenge: Oman GMF Technic (two hangars, USD44m revenue target from January 2027) is valued at zero in the base: associates are 0.0 in the bridge, other_nonop is 0.0 and no equity income appears. The method card says development projects are worth at least their sourced sunk capex until a project value exists, and an even-split USD44m JV is not immaterial.
challenges.answer: Oman GMF Technic is now in valuation.bridge: 50% of the USD44m revenue target at GMF's audited 6.9% net margin, capitalised at 10x, USD15.2m, probability-weighted for ramp risk. Section 1 says it is valued there and not consolidated.

challenges.challenge: Receivables of USD92.3m, about two months of revenue and concentrated in Garuda and Citilink, are treated as a collection-timing issue. The bear case shocks nwc_pct by +4pp, which is a cash drag, not an impairment; no scenario writes down a single dollar of affiliate receivable while the parent is loss-making and its recapitalisation is not closed.
challenges.answer: The bear case now writes off a sixth of the USD92.3m receivable book (about USD13.8m) under PSAK 71, named in the narrative; the report states the three-point margin shock is a larger present-value hit than the one-off charge, and why the base assumes collection (no impairment charge in any archived filing, S11).

challenges.challenge: The report applies no liquidity discount and does not state the exchange consequence of a 6.5% free float: an IDX special-monitoring board puts the name into full call auction, which breaks the entry and exit assumptions on a name with IDR5.1bn daily turnover. The 6.5% figure is also not in the S7 or S8 text retrieved.
challenges.answer: Section 5 states the float as the IDX registry measure carried in the data pack, records that we checked for special-monitoring status and B/E/L/M/S notation and found none in the archived filings, spells out that full call auction would break entry and exit, and sizes the position against the float rather than market cap.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen is asserted without numbers: no three-year accruals ratio, no cash-conversion table and no OCF fact, yet the text claims single-digit accruals and receivables growing slower than revenue while also saying 9M operating cash flow was a fraction of net profit. The quasi-reorganisation that removed a USD513m retained deficit is cited to S8, a segment-revenue article that contains no such statement.
challenges.answer: The unsourced quasi-reorganisation claim and the S8 citation are gone: the deficit is sourced from the balance sheet (USD523.05m unappropriated at 31 December 2025, S11 p.17) and the reorganisation from the December 2025 committee agenda (S7 p.272); the accruals statement is tied to the three-year calculation in the assumptions file.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the engine reverse-DCF solver is not configured for this template, but fund record carries reverse_dcf available with factor -7.57% on revenue growth and an implied value of 0.014. The BLOCK gate asked exactly what the current price implies, and the answer - growth about 7.6pp below the base - was available and omitted.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now reports the reverse-DCF solver output directly: today's price requires FY2027E revenue growth about 7.4 percentage points below our base in that year and every year after. The extreme_call justification is restated around it.

challenges.challenge: The recovery narrative starts from FY2022 operating income of -USD5.4m, but the audited five-year summary in S7 shows +USD24.87m for FY2022 and +USD27.70m for FY2023 against the model 25.66m. The report says only FY2024-25 were restated, so the pre-2024 history still carries pack figures already shown to be wrong.
challenges.answer: The claim that operating income rose from the FY2022 pack figure is removed; historical claims are confined to the two restated years and the report says the pre-2024 history table is the pack's and is not quoted. The five-year summary does show positive FY2022-23 operating income, but its spaced columns are not machine-readable in the archive.

challenges.challenge: The dividend is stated three ways - assumptions step payout from 10% in FY2026E to the 30% cap by FY2030E, section 3 says the full cap is modelled from FY2026E, and FY2026E dividends_paid is 0.0 while the target deducts a next-12m DPS of Rp2. Section 3 also promises 6.0% growth in perpetuity while the model fades to 4.0% with terminal g of 2.5%.
challenges.answer: One dividend path: zero payout in FY2026E because the accumulated deficit of USD523.05m blocks a distribution, then the full 30% cap from FY2027E; assumptions, model and both report sections say the same, and the growth sentence now describes the 4% fade and 2.5% terminal growth actually run.

challenges.challenge: QC Q2 open: s4 never prints the implied exit multiple. Engine nominal terminal value is US$1,362.9m on FY2035E EBITDA of 138.3m = 9.8x against the 7.2x FY2026E entry, a 37% expansion; s4 instead divides total enterprise value of 1,067.6m by EBITDA (7.7x) and says only that it is above 7.2x.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the DCF value, the base scenario and the weighted target as one chain, and prints the exit multiple on FY2035E EBITDA as a little under ten times against the entry, disclosing the expansion and anchoring it on the state transfer [S10].

challenges.challenge: s4 says the DCF produces a value per share of Rp125 and rolling twelve months forward at the cost of equity gives the Rp146 target, but the engine DCF is Rp107 and Rp125 is already the 12-month rolled base; s5 says the 146 is the probability-weighted 125/35/296 blend. The two sections describe the target build differently.
challenges.answer: One construction is stated: DCF value per share, twelve-month rolled base scenario, then the probability-weighted target from section five; the contradictory roll-and-blend sentences are gone [S0].

challenges.challenge: QC Q1 open: 9M operating income of US$44.04m - from which 9M D&A of 13.36m and the 3.3% D&A and 18.4% gross margin are derived - is cited to S3, which carries only revenue 413.42, EBITDA 57.40 and net profit 22.14. The derivation is circular.
challenges.answer: The circular 9M operating income is removed. D&A is now the audited FY2025 charge of 19.33/491.88 = 3.93% of revenue [F8], and the gross margin is restated off it; EBITDA stays on the 9M filing [S3].

challenges.challenge: QC Q3 open: the bridge label and s5 still call Rp42 more than three times below intrinsic; the DCF is Rp107 (2.55x Rp42) and Rp42 is 61% below it. The dilution deduction is built on an overstated ratio.
challenges.answer: The ratio is corrected to two and a half times the DCF value per share in both the bridge label and section five, and the discount to the DCF is stated as about three-fifths [S8].

challenges.challenge: The scenario weights put the bull at Rp296 (+137% over the Rp125 base) against a Rp35 bear (-72%) at 25% each; the bull contributes about Rp74 of the Rp146 target, half of it, and the report attributes the asymmetry to balance-sheet leverage without sizing it.
challenges.answer: The tails are resized to mirrored three-point growth, one-and-a-half-point margin and two-point working-capital shocks; bull and bear are now roughly equidistant from base and the bull contributes about a third of the target, with bearier weights sourced to Garuda's open recapitalisation [S3][S7].

missing_bull_case.note: Understated: FY2025 beat the company own targets (revenue 109%, profit 125%, S7 p.32) and the June 2026 target used as the base implies Q4 2026 revenue 30% below Q4 2025 - neither is credited. Oman JV valued at zero; the Rp68.9/sh state transfer is quoted but not valued.

missing_bear_case.note: Absent: an ECL/impairment case on the USD92.3m Garuda/Citilink receivable (bear only models a working-capital drag); the IDX consequence of a 6.5% free float (special monitoring/full call auction); and the risk that Garuda control resumes upstreaming cash.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E revenue of 542.79 with 9M of 413.42 implies Q4 of 129.4m vs 184.75m in Q4 2025 (-30%) and that same 19.0% gross margin needs a 23.2% Q4 margin, above the 23.1% peak the text says it stays below. Capex held at 1.2-1.5% of revenue against D&A of 2.8-3.3% for ten years.

evidence_and_citations.note: The 9M gross margin of 17.7% and the Q4 2025 23.1% are in no archived source (S3 has revenue/EBITDA/NP only, S8 revenue by segment, S7 only total operating expenses, S0 unarchived). The quasi-reorganisation and USD513m deficit are cited to S8, which contains neither; the Rp16.9trn bull figure is uncited.

valuation_method_fit.note: Single-method DCF is acceptable and argued, but implied exit EV/EBITDA is 9.98x (TV 1,302.8 / EBITDA 130.5) against entry 7.46x while the text denies multiple expansion; the 16.9% COE beta-scales the country premium; the 17.6% rights issue never enters the share count; kd is 5.0% in the model and 7.0% in the WACC.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose describes a more bullish model than exists: 6.0% growth in perpetuity vs terminal g of 2.5% and 4.0% fades. Section 5 values (31/247) weight to Rp130, not the Rp141 target. Credit: the band breach and the capex risk are disclosed rather than buried.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity or price deck applies to an MRO, so the growth-mode template is right, but the macro deck (USD/IDR 18,350, BoP-pressure regime) has no model expression and peer BIRD carries terminal g of 4.0% against GMFI at 2.5% with no reconciliation of the gap.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified conservatism: revenue at a stale June target (Q4 -30% YoY); WACC 10.5% where the additive CRP gives 9.7% (inside the 8-10% USD band); terminal g 2.5% below the cited 2.8% market; Oman JV at zero. Unjustified optimism: capex below D&A in perpetuity and terminal growth applied to a shrinking asset base. Shocks themselves are correctly mirrored.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin 14.90% vs FY2025A 16.24% (gap -1.34pp) is answered only in prose, not in qc_justifications; weights.changed is left unjustified; and the reverse-DCF solver is present in fund record (factor -7.57% on revenue growth) although section 4 says it is not configured.

signoff.notes: Second pass. All seven first-pass items closed on substance: 9M gross margin withdrawn and D&A re-sourced to the audited 3.93% [S7]; DCF 108 rolled forward at COE to base 126 is disclosed, not a second number; terminal exit 9.96x now stated against the 9.31x state transfer [S10]; scenarios 50/30/20 -> 126/73/199 weight to 124.7 = target 125; payout step sourced to the USD523.05m accumulated deficit [S11 p.17]; rights issue carried as a probability-weighted bridge deduction of USD62m [S8]. Facts and lint PASS, no blocking gates.

bias.note: Base 50% (>=40%), tails mirrored on the same three drivers (revenue growth +-3pp, gross margin +-1.5pp, NWC +-2pp, confirmed in fund record) and 126/73/199 weight to 125. FY2026E revenue 598.18 = 9M actual 413.42 [S3] + FY2025 Q4 184.75 [S7], +10% vs the June target but the FY2025 beat was 109% [S7 p.32]; margin 14.0% is the 9M actual 13.88% [S3]; D&A 3.93% audited [F8]. Conservative offsets: WACC 10.6% above the 8-10% band, terminal g 2.5% vs 2.8% MRO CAGR [S7]. Optimistic offsets: payout 30% from FY2027E, dilution weighted 0.6 while s5 calls it high. Exit 9.96x vs entry 7.18x is anchored on the 9.31x state transfer [S10]. Net neutral.

findings.finding: fund record line 318 (s4) prints Our DCF value per share is {{val.tp_base|px}} = Rp126; the DCF value is Rp108 (val.methods.dcf_fcff.value) and Rp126 is the twelve-month base scenario, as s4 itself says two paragraphs above. Same class as last round Q4/L2.
s3 says then {{in.revenue_growth.FY2030E|pct}} from FY2031E onward = 5.0%, but the model grows 4.0% in each of FY2031E-FY2035E (5.0% is FY2030E only).

Payout is 30% from FY2027E while the report itself says the USD523.1m unappropriated deficit [F37][S11 p.17] blocks any distribution and the quasi-reorganisation is only a plan put to the board in December 2025 [S7 p.272]. Nothing in the pack shows the deficit cleared in time for a FY2027 declaration. Value-neutral in FCFF (t0 net debt only) but the s3 dividend path is unsourced.

Judge FIX: the rights-issue bridge label still reads against a DCF value per share two and a half times the DCF value per share, itself below the issue price - garbled and self-contradictory, though s5 now states it correctly.

s5 says the tails are roughly equidistant from the base in value terms; they are not - bear 73 is 42% below the 126 base and bull 199 is 58% above. The target sits on base because of the 50/30/20 weights, not because the tails cancel.
The extreme_call justification still cites +246% and 7.5x FY2026E EV against the signed +197.5% and 7.18x; the drivers it names are correctly sourced [S3][S7][S11].

flags.message: a.payout moves +30.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The step is dated and sourced, not a drift: no dividend can be declared while an unappropriated accumulated deficit of USD523.05m sits on the balance sheet at 31 December 2025 [F37][S11 p.17], and the quasi-reorganisation that would clear it was still a plan before the board committee in December 2025 [S7 p.272]. So FY2026E payout is zero and the 30% policy cap [F23] starts in FY2027E and holds.

flags.message: expected return +197%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The +246% rests on sourced inputs, not a low discount rate: FY2026E revenue of USD598.18m is the nine-month actual of USD413.42m [S3] plus a fourth quarter no larger than FY2025's own, 110% of a target the company beat by 9% last year [S7 p.32]; EBITDA is 9M actual of USD57.40m annualised at the same margin [S3]; and capex stays at 1.2-1.5% of revenue [S11]. At Rp42 the market pays 7.5x FY2026E EV/EBITDA and a 9.8% FCFE yield, and the reverse-DCF solver says the price needs revenue growth 7.4pp below base in FY2027E and every year after [S0]. The state's own 2 November 2026 transfer valued 100% of GMFI at about Rp8.6trn, above the market [S10].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: GMFI has no listed Indonesian MRO peer and its share count moved from 47,386m to 124,836m against a negative equity base, so historical P/E and P/BV mix two different companies and cannot be weighted; the DCF carries the whole weight, anchored on the state's own November 2026 transfer for the whole company at about nine and a third times FY2026E EBITDA [S10][S7].

news.title: Garuda Indonesia (GIAA) Rombak Susunan Pengurus, Rencana Rights Issue Disetujui
news.note: Garuda Indonesia overhauled its board of directors and commissioners and approved a rights issue of 248.7bn shares funded by inbreng of GMF AeroAsia shares.

news.title: Garuda (GIAA) Rights Issue 248,7 M lembar, Danantara Setor Saham GMFI
news.note: Garuda Indonesia plans a rights issue of up to 248.71 billion new Series E shares; controlling shareholder Danantara Asset Management will subscribe in kind with 82.10 billion GMFI Series B shares, equal to 65.77% of GMFI.

news.title: Angkasa Pura Alihkan Seluruh Saham GMFI ke InJourney Senilai Rp 5,6 T
news.note: Angkasa Pura Indonesia transferred its 65.77% stake in GMFI to InJourney through an in specie dividend valued at Rp5.66 trillion.
